complexity_rationale: Backend-only (/api). Closely mirrors established job patterns already in the codebase: OfferTimeoutJob/StalePositionJob (RunTickAsync + thin PeriodicTimer shell, per-order fresh scope + CurrentTenant.FleetId, (int?)-cast FleetSettings projection guard), Common/Geo/HaversineDistance, OrderService/OrderStateMachine New->Assigned, order_events-derived exclusion set. No new architecture, no new entity (FleetSettings already carries AutoDispatchEnabled/AutoDispatchAfterSeconds/MaxOfferRadiusKm). Real logic (nearest-first selection, exclusion, optimistic-concurrency race with manual assign) but all precedented -> moderate, NOT novel; no kit specialists.
key_constraints: All status changes via OrderService/OrderStateMachine — NEVER set order.Status directly (read taxi-order-state-machine skill). Mirror OfferTimeoutJob EXACTLY: internal RunTickAsync + thin ExecuteAsync PeriodicTimer shell; scan in one scope with IgnoreQueryFilters projecting (OrderId,FleetId,PickupLat,PickupLng); per-order fresh scope resolving concrete CurrentTenant + set FleetId + resolve OrderService (one scope per order so a poisoned change-tracker doesn't leak). (int?)-cast projection on FleetSettings.MaxOfferRadiusKm/AutoDispatchAfterSeconds (missing row must NOT default to 0 — skip instead). Eligibility: same fleet, online/available (not Offline, not on active ride), fresh position (StalePositionJob threshold), within MaxOfferRadiusKm (Common/Geo/HaversineDistance.Meters); exclude drivers already offered+declined/timed-out for THIS order (derive from order_events driver ids). Nearest among remaining. Sequential nearest-first emerges from existing OfferTimeoutJob revert (no new timeout logic). Optimistic-concurrency Version guards manual-assign race (conflict caught+skipped, no exception surfaced). Tenant isolation integration test (fleet A dispatch never touches fleet B). Logging: Information on assign (OrderId/DriverId/FleetId), Debug 'no eligible driver' with Reason, no PII. DI hosted service alongside OfferTimeoutJob, ~5s poll. dotnet build -warnaserror + dotnet test (Testcontainers, Docker up; ephemeral ports so host-postgres:5432 conflict does NOT affect dotnet test). No frontend change.
